author: agent-3
reviewStatus: AUTHORED SOLO in response to A2's v1.1 rejection. Not re-reviewed.
purpose: Close R-1 item (1) — core lifetime-neutrality — by defining the execution-core boundary, removing the duplicate storage authority, making ambient authority mechanically detectable, and correcting two over-claiming tests.

resolves.A2-R1-06 / A2-R1-V11-01: Execution-core boundary defined explicitly. Five previously unresolved authorities are each placed INSIDE (injected) or OUTSIDE (forbidden), with a reason. CoreDeps is no longer asserted exhaustive by fiat; exhaustiveness is now a consequence of the boundary plus LN-11's closure test.
resolves.A2-R1-V11-02: LN-02 rewritten. It no longer claims completeness from a field list. LN-11 adds import/call-closure analysis and LN-12 adds runtime denial of ambient authority — the two methods that can detect what a field list cannot.
resolves.A2-R1-V11-03: LN-06 corrected: both stores carry byte-identical authoritative ledger, baseline, evidence and derivation inputs, differing ONLY in disposable acceleration entries. The prior populated-vs-empty comparison could not distinguish a lifetime bug from missing authoritative data.
resolves.A2-R1-V11-04: LN-09 corrected: the required outcome set now permits a typed busy-timeout after bounded retries. The prior 'both succeed' assertion over-claimed liveness the storage protocol never promised.
resolves.A2-R1-06.signatureDefect: Duplicate storage authority removed. StoreHandle is supplied ONLY through CoreDeps; the analyze signature no longer takes it separately.

decisionDependencies.claim: four separable decisions; only core lifetime-neutrality closable now
contention resolved by busy-timeout, idempotent insert, write-then-link — integrity, not liveness
warm state is an acceleration, never an evidence authority
equality only for deterministic producers under identical identities and exact Coverage
LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT is a typed operational termination distinct from corruption

executionCoreBoundary.definition: The execution core takes a sealed Snapshot and a validated Plan and produces a SealedRun. It performs no admission, no resolution, and no supervision.

inside.authority: fact derivation, rule evaluation, policy evaluation

inside.why: Budgets are Plan inputs and their exhaustion is Coverage, which the core must produce.

outside.why: InvocationPlan work (c2-plan-stage-schema.v2). The core receives resolved identities.
Grants are fixed in PlanId before the core runs. A core that could grant could escalate.
Probe and scanner execution is supervised OUTSIDE the core. Placing a process supervisor inside would give the core spawn authority, defeating LN-12.
Host concerns. Their absence from the core is what makes lifetime-neutrality meaningful.

injectedNotAmbient.resolution: INJECTED and deterministic. RunId/ExecutionId are content-derived or supplied. Ambient random generation defeats replay and every equality test.
INJECTED as a resolved, immutable map. A Plan names work by identity; resolution happened outside. The core cannot look anything up.
INJECTED. The core requests execution through a supplied scheduler; it does not create threads or processes itself.
INJECTED and bounded. A no-op sink must be valid and must not change results (LN-10).
OUTSIDE the core entirely — see `outside`. Probe execution is host-supervised; the core receives observations as inputs.

exhaustiveness.why: v1.1 asserted CoreDeps exhaustive, which A2 correctly rejected: a field list cannot prove the absence of unlisted ambient access. Exhaustiveness is now the CONCLUSION of LN-11 and LN-12, not a premise.

coreApi.signature: analyze(snapshot: SealedSnapshot, plan: ValidatedPlan, deps: CoreDeps) -> SealedRun
coreApi.changeFromV1_1: StoreHandle removed from the positional signature. It is supplied only via CoreDeps, so there is exactly one storage authority path (A2-R1-06).
explicitlyAbsent: process-global singletons, ambient scope, thread-local context
process spawn, network, or filesystem access of any kind

conformanceTests.assert: Two core instantiations in one process with disjoint deps produce results with no observable interference.
The core constructs only when every CoreDeps member is supplied. Omitting any is a construction-time error, never a silent ambient fallback.
conformanceTests.note: REWRITTEN: this now claims only what it can prove — no fallback for LISTED members. Completeness is LN-11/LN-12's job.

conformanceTests.assert: Concurrent Plans for different ProjectIds with distinct storage authorities produce independent SealedRuns.
The core's public surface contains no parameter, field, or environment read distinguishing a one-shot from a resident host. Provable with no resident host in existence.
Two sequential invocations in one process with identical Snapshot, Plan, toolchain and environment identities and identical exact Coverage yield byte-identical EvidenceDigests.

Two invocations against stores carrying BYTE-IDENTICAL authoritative ledger, baseline, evidence and derivation inputs, differing only in disposable acceleration entries, yield byte-identical EvidenceDigests. The core cannot observe store implementation, cache warmth, hit rate, or entry presence except through fact/CAS operations whose semantic result is identical.
conformanceTests.note: CORRECTED per A2-R1-V11-03. The prior populated-vs-empty form could not distinguish a lifetime bug from absent authoritative data.

conformanceTests.assert: Cancelling the supplied token terminates the attempt with an honest terminal or abandoned state — never a sealed passing empty Run — and leaves no orphaned child process.

Two concurrent Plans for the SAME ProjectId and storage authority: EACH contender either publishes one valid SealedRun or returns a typed LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT after bounded retries. Every successful write remains reachable. No corrupt, partial, or lost publication is observable.
conformanceTests.note: CORRECTED per A2-R1-V11-04. Integrity is guaranteed; liveness for both contenders is not, and the protocol never promised it.

conformanceTests.assert: Results and EvidenceDigest are identical whether a recording or a no-op progress/diagnostics sink is supplied.

CLOSURE ANALYSIS: the import/call closure of the execution core reaches no filesystem, network, process-spawn, environment, ambient-random, signal-handler, thread-local, or global-registry API. A reachable one is a finding even if unused at runtime.
conformanceTests.note: NEW per A2-R1-V11-02. This is the method that detects what a field list cannot — and it is the same method that caught two earlier capability errors in this exercise.

conformanceTests.assert: RUNTIME DENIAL: with ambient authorities revoked or stubbed to fail, the core completes a representative Plan successfully. Any attempt to reach environment, filesystem, network, spawn, or ambient entropy fails the test.
The core produces identical RunId/ExecutionId for identical inputs when supplied a deterministic ID source, proving no ambient entropy participates in identity.

productObligationsNotClosedHere.obligation: A full-capability one-shot host must exist for CI, offline use, and recovery.
productObligationsNotClosedHere.why_separate: A product/deployment obligation, not evidence of core re-entrancy.

sealedPropertiesCovered.property: warm state is an acceleration, never an evidence authority
any evidence-writing host is multi-process safe (integrity, not liveness)
equality only for deterministic producers under identical identities
crash/cancel never yields a passing empty Run
no ambient authority in the core

peerReviewRequired: Is placing the external-process supervisor OUTSIDE the core correct? It means Probe observations enter the core as inputs, which may be the wrong factoring if probes need to interleave with fact derivation.

Is LN-11's closure analysis achievable for a core that necessarily links a storage library, which itself touches the filesystem? The boundary may need to be drawn at the StoreHandle interface rather than at the link graph.
LN-13 assumes content-derived or injected identity. Does that hold for ExecutionId, which is allocated at admission before content is known?
knownLimitations: A conformance specification, not an implemented suite.

LN-11 has a real tension noted in peer review: a storage dependency legitimately touches the filesystem, so the closure boundary probably has to be the StoreHandle interface. This artifact does not resolve that and it may weaken LN-11 materially.
Nothing here measures performance. R-1 items (2)-(4) are untouched by a passing suite.
Authored solo; the boundary placement of five authorities is judgment, and A2 explicitly flagged medium confidence on which side each belongs.

priorFindingDispositions.A2-R1-03: PARTIAL in v1 — LN-09 exercised the right contention case but over-asserted liveness. CLOSED by the corrected LN-09 required-outcome set permitting typed LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT.
priorFindingDispositions.A2-R1-04: ACCEPT in v1 — deterministic equality preconditions explicit. Retained and extended to LN-06.
priorFindingDispositions.A2-R1-05: ACCEPT in v1 — cachePolicy removal correct. Retained; explicitlyAbsent now also bars any lifetime discriminator.
priorFindingDispositions.A2-R1-06: REJECT in v1.1 — CoreDeps not exhaustive, two storage authorities. CLOSED: duplicate StoreHandle removed from the positional signature; exhaustiveness withdrawn as a premise and made a conclusion of LN-11/LN-12.
priorFindingDispositions.A2-R1-07: ACCEPT in v1 — decision source paths resolvable. Retained.
priorFindingDispositions.A2-R1-08: ACCEPT in v1 — one-shot availability separated as a product obligation. Retained as PO-01.
